A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 18-page ClearSight paper, including supplementary Sections 8–10. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the manuscript, equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention analyses, VAF benchmark evaluations, inference measurements, ablations and qualitative case studies in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons in Section 6 and additional experiments and ablations in Sections 8–9.

M1.justification: Section 5 retains identical visual-attention amplification, system-prompt suppression and selection of the top 50% of visually attentive heads. The algorithm and equations are unchanged.

E1.justification: Coverage remains POPE on MSCOCO, A-OKVQA and GQA, plus MME, NoCaps, ScienceQA and LLaVA-Bench. No evaluated datasets, tasks or scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Regular decoding, VCD and ICD retain their participation in the corresponding main-text comparisons. Comparator membership in the supplementary experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both versions report identical backbones, evaluation metrics, greedy-decoding comparisons, 500-example attention analysis and default alpha=0.15 and beta=0.1 settings. Supplementary evaluation procedures also match.

E4.justification: The coefficient, layer-selection, visual-perception-head and sampling-strategy analyses remain identical, as do the LLaVA-Bench case studies in Section 8.4.

E5.justification: Statistical and uncertainty reporting is unchanged throughout both PDFs. No run-count, seed, interval, error-bar or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative examples are unchanged. Tables 6 and 9 alter visual emphasis only; their values and numerical rankings remain identical.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same decoding formulation, saliency measures, attention-allocation definitions and modification masks. No mathematical reasoning or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about visual neglect, hallucination mitigation and preservation of generation quality and inference speed.

C2.justification: Interpretations of modality fusion and visual neglect are identical. Discussions of adverse effects from excessive amplification or suppression in Sections 6.3 and 9 are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Parameter disclosures, the A800 80G hardware description, decoding details, prompt templates and code-access statement and link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research positioning and all 55 numbered references are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 17 March 2025 to v2 dated 27 May 2025. Manuscript prose, headings and section organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Tables 6 and 9 change VAF precision and recall entries from bold red to regular black, retaining emphasis on accuracy and F1. Figures, captions, table structures and surrounding layout are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The table-formatting revision removes misleading best-score emphasis. For example, Table 6 in v1 highlights VAF precision of 92.9 despite VCD scoring 94.4; v2 removes that highlight. This modestly improves presentation accuracy, although precision/recall winners are now unmarked and the captions remain unchanged. Scientific methods, evidence and claims are identical.
